messages:
Maya (Sales): Customer asked for a short on-prem POC checklist + how we handle hosted fallback keys and Dedicated pool billing. They want private control plane in their VPC and minimal outbound egress. Can we summarise exact network + node preflight items they must run?
Ravi (Platform): Short answer: we support private control plane in-customer-VPC. Network: outbound TLS to our collector endpoints only, allowlist of static egress IPs, and either VPC peering or TGW. We'll need their firewall to allow 443 outbound to these FQDNs: collector.redwood.example, metrics.redwood.example.
Priya (Infra): Node preflight checklist (concise): kernel >=5.15, nvidia driver >=525 (we prefer 535+ for Ampere/Blackwell), CUDA runtime >=11.8 (12.x recommended for latest quantized runtimes), nvidia-container-toolkit installed, kubelet cgroup driver=systemd, docker/containerd configured with nvidia runtime.
Ravi (Platform): Commands they can paste back: `uname -r`, `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv,noheader`, `lsmod | grep nvidia`, `kubectl get nodes -o wide`, `cat /var/log/nvidia-installer.log` and `systemctl show -p ExecMainStatus nvidia-persistenced`.
Maya (Sales): Great. Also need a short template I can send to the customer's infra ops asking for those outputs plus their preferred Dedicated sizing (number of GPUs) so we can quote hourly vs 7-day fixed.
Priya (Infra): Template snippet: "Please run and paste outputs: `uname -r`, `nvidia-smi -L`, `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv,noheader`, `kubectl get nodes -o wide`, `cat /etc/containerd/config.toml` (or docker daemon), and confirm `nvidia-container-toolkit` version."
Noah (Security): Security follow-ups: they asked about customer-managed KMS for disk encryption, audit logs retention >=90d, SOC2 report, and whether control-plane <-> node traffic is mTLS. Answer: private mode supports CMK (we'll need IAM policy/ARN), audit logs can be exported and retained 90+ days, we can share SOC2 report under NDA, and control-plane connections use mTLS. They also want evidence of image vulnerability scans.
Maya (Sales): Can you drop a one-liner for me to include on SOC2 and vuln scanning please?
Noah (Security): One-liner: "We can provide our SOC2 Type II summary under NDA and a sanitized vulnerability scan export for the images used in the installer; our release images go through SCA and CVE scanning and we maintain a tracked remediation backlog."
preflight-bot: preflight v2.2 ran at 2026-03-03T09:41:12Z 00. Results: connectivity OK to collector endpoints, node-02 shows missing `nvidia-container-toolkit`, node-04 reports driver 470 (needs upgrade), kubelet on node-03 cgroup driver= cgroupfs (should be systemd). See /preflight/1799012345/report.
Priya (Infra): Action items: 1) Customer to run Ravi's commands and paste outputs. 2) Upgrade driver on node-04 to >=525 or set driver to 535 if available. 3) Install nvidia-container-toolkit on node-02. 4) Set kubelet cgroup driver to systemd on node-03 and restart kubelet. 5) Sales to confirm expected GPU count so we can produce hourly vs committed 7-day pricing sketch.
Maya (Sales): I'll email the checklist + the security one-liner and ask them to confirm GPU count and whether they want a fixed 7-day commitment or hourly billing. I'll attach the preflight report link. Will follow up once they paste outputs. Thanks folks. :raised_hands:
